source: hand-verified from the book's own CONTENTS (body lines 131-153)
notes: The shipped detection is 3 chapters — 9,984 / 173,461 / 29,196 words — because the bare-numeral pattern matched the Latin initials in 'D. OCTAVIUS CAESAR AUGUSTUS.' and in the monumental inscription 'M. AGRIPPA. L. F. COS: TERTIUM. FECIT.'. The book's contents list three parts: I. the twelve Caesars, II. Lives of the Grammarians and Historians, III. Lives of the Poets (six named), then FOOTNOTES and INDEX. exact_count is deliberately null: whether the appended Lives should be one chapter each or one per part is a judgment call this fixture does not pretend to settle. What is not a judgment call is that each of the twelve Caesars is its own chapter and the inscription is not a heading.
